customManagers.description: Versions marked with a `# renovate:` comment — CI tool pins and the ansible fresh-install baseline (k3s, kube-vip, MetalLB)
k3s version in the system-upgrade-controller Plans — the field that actually drives a live cluster upgrade

description: AUTOMERGE, tier 1: app updates that Flux applies through a HelmRelease (the chart, and the images in its values) under kubernetes/apps. Docs: docs/updates.md.

Only these can automerge, because only these have a way back: Helm rolls back a failed upgrade, the rollout-guard soak check watches the release for 45m, and rollout-revert reverts the PR. Raw manifests (the `kubernetes` manager: redis.yaml, gotenberg, CronJobs) get none of that.
Everything outside kubernetes/apps (infrastructure, k3s and the SUC Plans, Flux, kube-vip, CI tool pins, ansible) never matches this rule, so it stays manual.

minimumReleaseAge 3 days: lets a broken release get pulled or patched first, and outlasts the 24h HelmRepository refresh, so a merged chart bump can't hit 'chart not found'. Paired with internalChecksFilter strict at the top level, which keeps the PR from being created until the 3 days have passed; otherwise GitHub auto-merge would merge it straight away.

Every rule below CARVES OUT an exception. Later rules win, and they set `labels` (which replaces) rather than `addLabels`, so an exception also drops the `automerge` label and the label always tells the truth.
The `automerge gate` check (.github/scripts/automerge-gate.py) independently re-checks paths, update types, quarantine and release-note wording before GitHub merges anything.

packageRules.description: DB-backed apps: patches only. A minor often runs schema migrations, and a migrated database can't be rolled back by reverting the image. Minors (and digest moves, which can hide one) stay manual.

description: Never automerge these apps:
authentik is SSO for everything; a bad rollout locks you out of the apps you'd use to fix it.
technitium must match the version on the VM primary (see its helmrelease.yaml), and DNS sits on the path the revert itself needs.
bambustudio fails silently (see the rule further down).
The monitoring platform IS the detection layer: the soak check reads its blackbox probes, and kube-prometheus-stack bumps carry CRDs.

packageRules.description: Home Assistant's monthly YYYY.M releases are 'minor' to Renovate but regularly carry backward-incompatible changes to integrations. Patches (YYYY.M.x) still automerge.
Datastore images never automerge, wherever they appear. tracearr runs Redis inside its own HelmRelease, so a path rule alone would miss it.
A digest move on a floating tag (seerr `latest@sha256`, sockpuppetbrowser `latest`) can hide a version jump of any size.

app-template is a shared library chart: one bump re-renders ~27 releases at once (including the DB apps and technitium), and its majors have changed immutable selectors before. Kept manual until rollout-revert has a track record.
0.x versions: a minor bump is a major bump (semver section 4).
Majors: separate PRs so breaking changes stand out. Never automerged. Last of the label-setting tier rules, so `type/major` survives.
Group app-template (bjw-s) chart bumps across the media apps
One PR for all digest pins instead of one per image — pinning is bookkeeping, not a decision

description: rancher/k3s-upgrade is written WITHOUT a tag in the system-upgrade-controller Plans, on purpose: the controller appends `.spec.version` as the tag when it creates the upgrade Job (v1.32.13+k3s1 -> :v1.32.13-k3s1).

Left enabled, the kubernetes manager would read it as an untagged image and offer to pin `:latest` — which would sever the version from the Plan and pin every future upgrade to whatever `latest` meant that day. The version is tracked through the `version:` field instead, above.

packageRules.description: CI tool pins are stored WITHOUT a leading `v` because the workflows add it when building the download URL. extractVersion keeps it that way, so a bump cannot silently produce `.../download/vv0.8.0/...`.
Renovate itself (the CI validator pin) releases several times a day. Monthly is plenty for a linter.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: kustomize lives in a monorepo and tags its releases `kustomize/vX.Y.Z`, alongside `api/…` and `cmd/config/…` tags for sibling modules.

description: k3s. Both places the version is written move together: the SUC Plans (which drive the live rolling upgrade) and the ansible inventory (the fresh-install/node-join baseline).
k3s versions look like v1.32.13+k3s1, which is not semver, hence the regex versioning.

separateMultipleMinor gives one PR PER MINOR STREAM rather than a single jump to the newest release. That matches the documented upgrade rule — k3s supports only +1 minor of skew, so 1.32 -> 1.36 must be walked one minor at a time, and four separate PRs is exactly that walk.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **Merging this upgrades the live cluster.** The system-upgrade-controller acts on every node labelled `k3s-upgrade=true` as soon as Flux applies the new Plan — control-plane nodes first, one at a time, cordoned but not drained. Run `kubectl get nodes -L k3s-upgrade` first to see how much of the cluster that is.
Take one minor at a time and let the cluster settle in between. Watch with `kubectl -n system-upgrade get jobs -w` and `kubectl get nodes -w`.

description: linuxserver/bambustudio is PINNED and Renovate is disabled for it. Every build after upstream's 2026-04-29 'rebase to resolute' is broken under containerd: Ubuntu 26.04's gdk-pixbuf 2.44 loads all images through glycin, glycin runs its loaders in `bwrap --unshare-all`, and bwrap's initial mount is denied by the containerd default AppArmor profile. GTK then fails to load an Adwaita SVG and aborts.

This is disabled rather than left to a review-each-PR rule because the failure is SILENT: the Selkies desktop still streams and the pod stays 1/1 Running with no restarts — only the browser shows a black screen, because Bambu Studio itself never starts. A merged bump would look completely healthy in every dashboard and alert we have.
Granting AppArmor Unconfined does NOT fix it (tested end-to-end — the loader still exits 1), so there is no securityContext escape hatch worth taking.

Re-enable once upstream ships a glycin/gdk-pixbuf fix. Verify by running the candidate tag and checking `ps aux | grep bin/bambu-studio` inside the pod. Keep the versioning regex below when re-enabling: Bambu's versions are zero-padded four-part, which default docker versioning cannot order.
MariaDB. The operator does not set MARIADB_AUTO_UPGRADE, so the on-disk system tables are NOT migrated automatically, and MariaDB cannot be downgraded in place.
Patch releases within a minor are routine; anything larger is a database migration.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **Database version change.** After the pod restarts on the new image, run `mariadb-upgrade` inside it by hand — the operator will not. There is no in-place downgrade, so take a dump first.

description: Falco Operator. Pre-1.0 with v1alpha1 CRDs, and it has already shipped one breaking API change (v0.1.x -> v0.2.0 required a migration guide). A 0.x bump here can change the schema of the Falco, Component, Config, Rulesfile and Plugin CRs in kubernetes/infrastructure/controllers/falco/config/.

CI cannot catch that: those kinds are absent from the datreeio CRD catalog, so kubeconform reports them as 'no schema, NOT validated' and the build stays green. A schema break surfaces as a stalled Flux Kustomization after merge, not as a red PR.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **Read the changelog before merging — do not rubber-stamp.** Diff the chart's `crds/` against the CRs in `kubernetes/infrastructure/controllers/falco/config/`, and check the [release notes](https://github.com/falcosecurity/falco-operator/releases) for a migration guide.

The OCI artifact versions (container plugin, falco-rules) are *not* managed by Renovate — they live in CRD fields rather than `image:` strings. Check them by hand against the `falco` chart's `containerEngine.pluginRef` when the bundled Falco version moves. See [`docs/falco-deploy.md`](docs/falco-deploy.md).

The same applies to the SECOND Falco instance in `kubernetes/infrastructure/controllers/falco-k8saudit/config/` (k8saudit plugin, k8saudit ruleset, json plugin). The k8saudit plugin and its ruleset must be bumped TOGETHER — the ruleset declares `required_plugin_versions` against an exact plugin version. See [`docs/falco-k8saudit.md`](docs/falco-k8saudit.md).
